newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour left-winger proposes socialist budget.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour left-winger proposes socialist budget.

text.p: The new Labour government should tax the rich, control corporate dividends and slash defence spending in its first budget, left-wing Labour member of parliament Ken Livingstone said on Tuesday.

In the latest edition of his Socialist Economic Bulletin Livingstone said Labour had inherited a 17.7 billion stg budget deficit that could usher in a deep public-sector financial crisis as the economy slows next winter due to rising interest rates and a strong pound.

Instead of making the average wage earner pay more tax, which would make it deeply unpopular, Labour should seek to curb excessive consumption by the wealthiest sections of society, Livingstone said. He proposed:
-- raising 10 billion pounds via the windfall tax on the monopoly profits of privatised utilities.
-- introducing controls on corporate dividends and halving relief on advanced corporation tax to 10 percent.
-- raising national insurance contributions on those earning more than 50,000 pounds a year.
-- reducing military spending to the western European average, to save two to three billion pounds a year.

"Labour will not be able to fudge these basic choices. They will determine the success or failure, and eventually the chances of re-election, of Tony Blair's first administration," Livingstone, who has sent the report to all Labour MPs, said.

Blair's masssive majority of 179 in the 659-seat House of Commons leaves him safe to ignore left-wingers like Livingstone, who are vastly outnumbered by the new intake of young, moderate Labour MPs loyal to Blair.
